Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
Acute presentation with one-day history of right-sided pleuritic chest/back pain, breathlessness, subjective fever, and two episodes of mild haemoptysis. Two-week history of fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance. On immunosuppressive therapy (Methotrexate) for SLE.

Consistent DDx considerations:
• Community-acquired pneumonia – high likelihood given acute fever, pleuritic pain, cough with haemoptysis, and immunosuppressed status.  
• Pulmonary embolism – moderate likelihood due to classic triad (pain, dyspnoea, haemoptysis) and underlying SLE, though no tachycardia or provoking factors noted.  
• Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis/alveolar haemorrhage – lower likelihood but considered because dose taken this morning.

Plan from transcript:
• Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for full vitals, chest auscultation, and blood pressure measurement.  
• Likely need for antibiotic therapy if pneumonia confirmed; clinician deferred prescribing until in-person assessment.  
• Consider chest X-ray and additional investigations (e.g., D-dimer/CTPA) depending on examination findings.  
• Provide patient with support line number to schedule appointment today.  
• Reassured patient that presentation is more suggestive of infection than lung cancer; further imaging may be arranged if symptoms persist.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Community-acquired pneumonia – High likelihood; matches acute fever, pleuritic pain, cough with blood-streaked sputum, immunosuppression.  
2. Pulmonary embolism – Moderate likelihood; triad present and SLE confers hypercoagulability, but normal pulse and absence of typical risk factors make it less likely.  
3. Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis/alveolar haemorrhage – Low-moderate likelihood; patient on Methotrexate, but presentation unusually abrupt.
